cells.tense: You are here before the choice is made, and nothing has collapsed yet.
cells.ask: Say one thing you want out loud, before you decide whether it's reasonable.
cells.core:
Something is at the start and hasn't been named. No plan, no direction — a moment where anything could still become anything, and you're letting it stay that way. Most people rush this part. They need to know what it is now. You can sit with it, pen in hand, before the words come.

Fairness runs alongside it. Two people look at the same mess; one calls it unfair right away, the other waits until the proportions are actually visible. Waiting is the harder move and the truer one. That's the shape of this: openness and a fair eye together, without rushing to name what isn't named. It's what lets the pull toward what matters show itself without your insisting it show the whole way today. Take it or leave it.
cells.sheetLine: You're in the open before anything is decided.
cells.verb: holding pure possibility open before anything has been chosen
cells.place: where what's out of proportion gets set back to fair

cells.tense: You are braced for a future where the choice will finally make itself clear.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you want and take its first step today — small, unfinished, no plan past tomorrow.
cells.core:
Every option stays open so none can become real. A choice feels like a loss, so you keep them all airborne and call it patience. You live in the version ahead — the one where you finally land, where it all adds up, where you'll know what you are. Meanwhile nothing gets made, and nothing here gets weighed fairly, because weighing requires deciding what counts.

Potential isn't a position you hold; it's a state you pass through. A seed doesn't stay a seed by being careful. You don't have to settle the whole life or find the one right answer. One thing you're genuinely drawn to, that no one asked you to want, is enough. Walk at it without needing to see the end. Being what you are takes no proving — it takes touching the ground.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping every door open and calling it patience.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that shut, and your hand is off the handle.
cells.ask: Write one plain page about where you stopped reaching — the setup, what you quit doing — and leave it unfinished.
cells.core:
The wide-open state underneath didn't leave. But something closed, and you stopped reaching for it. Now you build from what's safe — from what you're certain won't fail, from the narrow place. In this room, fairness has been keeping score, and lately the score has gone against you.

Don't push directly at what closed. Effort aimed at a shut place only confirms it's shut. The way back runs sideways: see the whole pattern once, without sorting it into blame or proof. It made sense when it happened, and it isn't the whole account. Let yourself know the shape and stop short of calling it final. When you can see where you narrowed, the narrowing loosens on its own. Being seen doesn't require being ready first.

cells.tense: You are weighing outcomes without noticing that you are the one weighing.
cells.ask: Find one spot today where the choice feels already made for you, and ask out loud whether it was.
cells.core:
You think this is just how it goes. Someone else decided, the system required it, there wasn't an option — while you're the one in it, moving things, measuring what's owed and what's fair. You don't see the measuring. A choice you don't see doesn't look like a choice. It looks like the shape of the situation.

Here's what you can use: that measuring instinct is real and it's yours. What's missing is checking whether anything else could have been there. No plan needed, no better answer. One look at a moment you'd swear had no choice in it, and an honest question of whether one existed. That's the whole move. The scale is in your hands, and it reads whatever you put on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're running the scale without seeing your hand on it.
